articles.title: Honda releases design sketches of first India-made electric SUV ahead of December 2 debut
articles.content: Honda ALPHA Honda Cars India has released exterior and interior design sketches of the Honda ALPHA , its first made-in-India electric SUV , ahead of its global premiere on December 2, 2026. Designed at Honda's Design Centre in Japan, the electric SUV will be unveiled in India. The company will disclose the model's complete details at the global premiere. The exterior sketch shows a sleek SUV silhouette with flowing proportions and a strong stance. Honda said the design combines a sophisticated appearance with a distinctive road presence. The interior sketch highlights a spacious cabin with a contemporary layout, smart technology and a focus on everyday convenience. The company said the design aims to offer a comfortable and intuitive experience for occupants. The Honda ALPHA marks an important milestone in the company's electrification strategy in India. Honda has not yet disclosed details such as battery capacity, driving range, powertrain or expected price. Earlier, Honda had said that the Alpha has been developed as an SUV combining advanced technology and futuristic design, with a focus on both urban and natural environments.

articles.title: West India's First SkyWalker Orthopedic Robotic System Launched at CURIS Hospital, Ahmedabad
articles.content: NewsVoir Ahmedabad (Gujarat) [India], November 25: CURIS Hospital, Ahmedabad, has become the first medical institution in Western India to introduce the SkyWalker Orthopedic Robotic System for knee replacement surgery, in collaboration with U.S.-headquartered MicroPort Orthopedics Inc. This landmark installation marks a significant advancement in the orthopedic care landscape across Gujarat and parts of Rajasthan, M.P. and Maharashtra, and is a moment of pride for both Ahmedabad and CURIS. SkyWalker is the only orthopedic robotic platform globally that is integrated with a patented True Medial-Pivot Knee philosophy, delivering sub-millimeter precision for highly accurate joint alignment. This technology enables superior stability, improved functional outcomes, and faster recovery—resulting in a durable, natural-feeling knee that allows patients to return more quickly to everyday activities such as walking long distances and climbing stairs with confidence and ease. “CURIS Hospital is defined by patient-centric care, continuous advancement, and a commitment to remain at the forefront of medical science,” said Ramesh Balasubramanian, Chairman & Founder, CURIS Hospital. “Healthcare innovation should never be limited by geography. At CURIS, our vision is not simply to introduce advanced technology, but to transform the way healthcare is experienced by patients. We believe that patients in Ahmedabad and across Western India deserve access to world-class medical technology, clinical expertise, and surgical excellence comparable to the best anywhere in the world. The launch of SkyWalker marks an important milestone in this journey, bringing greater precision, innovation, and the promise of better patient outcomes closer to home—empowering patients to regain mobility, independence, and confidence without having to travel far for advanced treatment.” Dr. Ajaysinh V Devda, Director of Orthopedic Department at CURIS Hospital, said “Entire Gujarat is witnessing significant rise in knee osteoarthritis— especially in elderly. Many of these patients are having bone-on-bone arthritis and severe deformities. Whether it is severe deformity or the more common case of knee osteoarthritis, patients seek total knee replacement surgery to regain mobility and independence. In this context, the SkyWalker Robotic System brings paradigm shift by supporting intelligent CT based patient specific planning capabilities and precise bone cutting through its proprietary Motion Follow technology, enabling accurate joint-line reconstruction with greater ease, reduced discomfort, and notably faster recovery.” SkyWalker is fully compatible with the Evolution® Medial-Pivot Knee System, which closely replicates natural knee kinematics. This combination overcomes long-standing challenges associated with conventional knee replacement—such as instability and residual pain. These two advanced technologies are designed to enhance clinical outcomes and boost overall patient satisfaction. “We believe that the real time dynamic gap balancing feature and built-in kinematic principles of SkyWalker allow complex cases to be managed far more effectively than traditional non-robotic techniques. It clearly stands apart from existing options, establishing a new patient-first benchmark in knee replacement surgery and elevating the overall surgical experience,” added Dr. Harshil Shah, Consultant, Orthopedics at CURIS. Dr. Mukesh Parmar, Managing Director and Senior General Manager for South Asia, MicroPort Orthopedics, commented, “We are privileged to introduce the SkyWalker system at CURIS, an institution committed to patient outcomes. articles.title: India Accelerates Geothermal Power Push - Construction World
articles.content: The National Policy on Geothermal Energy, notified in September 2025, provides a framework for exploration, development and utilisation. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) is responsible for implementing the policy, which also supports research, drilling, reservoir management, direct-use applications and the creation of a national geothermal data repository. The Geological Survey of India (GSI) has mapped 381 hot springs and identified 10 geothermal provinces, including the Himalayan, Naga-Lusai, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Son Narmada Tapi, West Coast, Cambay Graben, Aravalli, Mahanadi, Godavari and South Indian Cratonic regions. India’s theoretical geothermal resource potential is estimated at nearly 10.6 GW, with 42 sites considered suitable for electricity generation and direct heat applications. Development received a boost in July 2026 when the ONGC Energy Centre commissioned India’s first two geothermal wells at Puga Valley in Ladakh. The wells, each 1,000 metres deep and located at an altitude of more than 14,000 feet, are intended to support reservoir evaluation and the development of a 1 MW demonstration power project. India is also pursuing cooperation with Australia, Iceland and Saudi Arabia, while pilot projects are examining applications in heating, agriculture and geo-tourism. The policy encourages Ground Source Heat Pumps (GSHPs), reuse of abandoned oil and gas wells and the establishment of Centres of Excellence. Commercial-scale generation has not yet been established, but resource assessments, research and international partnerships are building the basis for wider deployment as India works towards its Net Zero target by 2070. India is stepping up efforts to develop geothermal energy as a dependable addition to its renewable power portfolio and reduce reliance on conventional fuels. The resource, generated by heat beneath the Earth’s surface, can provide electricity continuously without depending on daylight or weather conditions. articles.title: Bangalore Watch Company Introduces India's First Wristwatch with a Locket - ANI News
articles.content: NewsVoir Bangalore (Karnataka) [India], November 25: Bangalore Watch Company returns to classic watchmaking after eight years with Epoch, a mechanical dress watch that brings back classic proportions, features a hand-wound Swiss Movement visible through a sapphire exhibition window, and introduces a locket-style case that can be personalised with a secret message. A message kept inside the watch, meant to stay with its owner for eternity. In 2018, Bangalore Watch Company debuted with the Renaissance Automatic, a dress watch that introduced the world to fine watchmaking from India. Since then, the brand has created watches around stories of modern India, spanning aviation, space, cricket and the outdoors. With Epoch, the brand returns to classic watchmaking. Unlike its earlier collections that take inspiration from aviation, or space, cricket and the outdoors. “For many owners, a watch becomes more than something they wear every day. It can hold memories, mark an important moment, or remind them of someone they love. The locket-style caseback on Epoch comes from this idea. It gives owners a place to keep a personal message, something that stays with the watch and becomes part of their story,” says Mercy Amalraj, Co-founder of Bangalore Watch Company. For this collection, the brand has developed a locket-styled case that is only seen in watches from the mid-1950s. The locket has two functions; opening the case allows the viewer to see the intricately finished hand wound movement through a Sapphire crystal window that is called an exhibition caseback, and also allows the owner to engrave a personalised message on the inner side of the locket. This case is known for its complexity in design and engineering, while allowing for the owner to make the watch as personal as it can be. “The Renaissance Automatic that we launched in 2018 was a complex wristwatch. It carried an exhibition caseback to view the automatic movement and also carried intricate dial work like applied indices and a beautiful sunburst pattern. For the Epoch, we have pushed ourselves further with a locket-case, sapphire window, with a hand-wound Swiss-made movement with intricate Geneva stripes and blued screws. The dial is also quite magical with a “sunrise” pattern that is a spin on the usual sunray that you see in most other watches. The hour-markers are pyramid-shaped appliqués with four surfaces that reflect light, while the hands are diamond-cut and rhodium-finished. The dial also features Breguet-style numerals with a rail-track running around the perimeter. I believe we have outdone ourselves with the Epoch, and I am sure our customers are going to love this,", says Nirupesh Joshi, Co-Founder of Bangalore Watch Company. The Epoch is available in two executions. A beautifully finished stainless-steel case in a champagne coloured dial, or a Rose Gold case with a Deep Anthracite dial. articles.title: Entire partners with Sarvam to bring sovereign AI coding to India - ET AI
articles.content: Industry 1 min read Entire partners with Sarvam to bring sovereign AI coding to India The partnership will allow developers to host code in India and run AI coding agents on Sarvam's models, keeping code and AI inference within the country. ETEnterpriseAI Desk ETEnterpriseAI Published On Nov 25, 2026 at 10:29 AM IST Set ETEnterpriseAI as your preferred source on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Representative image Entire, the developer platform founded by former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke , has partnered with Sarvam to launch what it calls India's first agent-native Git forge with data residency . The partnership will enable developers to host code locally in India and run AI coding agents using Sarvam's models, keeping both code and AI inference within the country. “With Sarvam, we’re bringing India its first sovereign agent-native Git forge. Every developer in India can now build, commit, and review code that stays in the country, run their agents on Sarvam’s models, and ship on the fastest Git infrastructure in production today,” said Thomas Dohmke, Entire CEO. Advt The integration brings Sarvam's models to Entire's platform Trails, which the company describes as a replacement for the traditional pull request. Available in preview, Trails brings together developer intent, code, agent sessions and review evidence throughout the software development process. AI coding agents can address review findings in an iterative loop, while human developers validate changes before merging. Developers can also create, migrate and host private repositories on Entire's distributed Git infrastructure, selecting India as their primary region and source of truth for data residency. “With Entire and Sarvam, an engineering team can host its code in India and run its agents on models we train and serve here. For enterprises that need their code to stay in India, that opens up agent-assisted development even for their most sensitive repositories,” said Vivek Raghavan, co-founder of Sarvam. Entire also highlighted performance benchmarks from its open-source tool ForgeMark. In tests involving simultaneous agent-driven pushes, its platform handled 355 pushes per second, compared with 29 for Cursor Origin, 10 for GitLab and four for GitHub. The company said its early Indian adopters include Infosys and Open Healthcare Network. articles.title: India's First Industry-Manufactured PSLV Set For Maiden Launch In First Quarter Of 2027
articles.content: Nov 25, 2026 | Updated 10:28 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . India's space sector is preparing for a historic milestone with the country's first fully industry-manufactured Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) targeting launch in the first quarter of 2027. The rocket, designated PSLV-N1, marks the first time private industry has taken responsibility for end-to-end production of India's workhorse launcher rather than merely supplying components to ISRO. ISRO Chairman Dr V Narayanan announced the timeline on 24 November at the India International Space Conclave in New Delhi. The rocket is being manufactured by a consortium comprising Hindustan Aeronautics Limited and Larsen & Toubro, which received an Rs 860 crore contract from NewSpace India Limited in September 2022 to build five PSLV-XL launch vehicles. The PSLV, often referred to as ISRO's workhorse, is an expendable medium-lift launch vehicle weighing approximately 320 tonnes. Since its first flight in 1993, the rocket has established a strong reliability record and has been used extensively for launching Indian and foreign satellites into various orbits. The move represents a significant shift in India's space manufacturing ecosystem, with the government transferring launch vehicle production to industry to enhance private-sector participation. PSLV-N1's original launch targets included the first quarter of 2026, but the timeline has since slipped to early 2027 as the consortium handles the complex manufacturing, assembly, integration and testing processes independently. Narayanan also emphasised that the government is fast-tracking satellite launches in collaboration with startups, noting that ISRO currently has only 56 space assets in orbit. The privatisation of PSLV production forms part of India's broader strategy to scale up its launch cadence and compete more effectively in the global commercial space market.
